## The Course, in Three Numbers

- The NBRC project is **70%** of your grade
- Homework (5 assignments) is **15%**
- Participation & attendance is **15%**

Full breakdown: [check out the online syllabus](../syllabus.html#grading-policy)

## Attendance & Participation

- Attendance tracked starting **Week 2**
- One free absence, no questions asked
- After that, it costs you. Give me a heads-up in advance if you know you'll
  miss one
- This is a lab-heavy course. You learn R by writing R, not by watching it

## AI Tools: Encouraged, With a Catch

- Using AI to help with your coding is expected, not frowned on
- But some evaluation is **oral and visual**, including presentations, code
  walkthroughs, and design critique
- You need to be able to explain and defend your own work
- Over-reliance shows up fast in those moments

## What *Is* Data?

- A spreadsheet is not the same thing as a dataset
- A dataset is not the same thing as a data product
- Discussion: where's the line, and why does it matter for this course?

## What Is Data Science?

The R4DS "whole game":

**import → tidy → transform ⇄ visualize ⇄ model → communicate**

- We'll touch every stage of this loop this semester
- Most of the course lives in transform/visualize, but the NBRC project
  forces you through the whole loop

## The Tools

- **R** is the language
- **Posit Cloud** is where we all code (no local install needed)
- **Quarto** turns code into reports, slides, and sites (this website is
  built with it)

No live coding today. That starts next week.
